mainTopic: Can coins be acquired or used through חליפין? The גמרא proves they cannot, brings supporting authorities, and answers challenges from a ברייתא about a money changer and from a משנה in קידושין.
overview: Earlier, רב פפא had said that a coin can be acquired through חליפין, the exchange done by handing over a cloth (סודר). The גמרא challenges him from a ברייתא about a trick for redeeming מעשר שני without adding the חומש. If coins could be acquired through חליפין, the ברייתא would have offered an easier method. Defending רב פפא would require imagining a man with no coins, no cloth and no land, which is not believable. So the גמרא concludes that coins are not acquired through חליפין, and a story shows that רב פפא himself came to act this way. עולא, רב אסי and רבי יוחנן all agree that a coin cannot be used for חליפין. רבי אבא challenges עולא from a ברייתא about borrowing from a money changer and paying back a little extra. That challenge is answered in two ways: the coins are unstamped פרוטטות that count as goods, or, according to רב אשי, having money at home makes it like 'lend me until I find the key.' Finally, the גמרא brings a משנה that seems to say a coin can be חליפין, and רב יהודה begins to explain it differently. His explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: redeeming on coins at home
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its case. After giving the produce to his friend, the owner says it is redeemed on coins he has at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And then he says: 'This produce is hereby redeemed on coins that I have at home.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of the ברייתא about the trick for redeeming מעשר שני. It ends with the owner redeeming the produce on coins that are sitting at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the ברייתא, the owner stands at the threshing floor with no money in hand and gives the produce to a friend as a gift. Now he redeems it on coins at home. Because the produce no longer belongs to him, he does not have to add the חומש. Every detail here, especially 'no money in hand,' will become the basis of the attack on רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeemed. The holiness of the produce moves onto the coins.
Coins, money
Second tithe. Produce that must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed on money.

phrases.english: And then he says:
phrases.notes: This is the owner, right after he has given the produce to his friend as a gift.

phrases.english: They are hereby redeemed
on coins that I have at home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote of the ברייתא from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner who gave away his produce can then redeem it on coins he has at home, and so avoid the חומש.

steps.title: Inference: with coins in hand, a better method exists
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the trick was only needed because he had no coins in hand. Had he coins with him, he would hand them to the friend through משיכה and let the friend redeem.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he does it this way is that he has no coins in his hand. But if he had coins in hand, he should give them to the other person by pulling, and that person would redeem the produce. That way is better, because the one redeeming is a stranger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a careful inference from the words 'no money in hand.' This sets up the coming challenge against רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner had coins with him, the best method would be to transfer them to the friend through משיכה (pulling), and then the friend redeems. That is preferable because the redeemer is a stranger, so it looks less like a trick. The ברייתא's emphasis on 'no money in hand' shows that only physical lack of coins forced the weaker method.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is. Used to draw an inference from a detail.
Pulling. A way of acquiring movable objects by drawing them toward oneself.
Better, preferable
A stranger, an outsider

phrases.english: The reason is that he has no coins in his hand,
but if he has coins in his hand –
let him transfer them to the other person by pulling
and that person redeems,
since this way is better,
since he is a stranger.
phrases.notes: He means the person doing the redeeming is an outsider, so it looks less like a trick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא would prefer giving coins to the friend if it were possible
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's wording 'עומד בגורן ואין בידו מעות'

steps.title: Challenge: why not transfer the coins with a cloth?
steps.stepSummary: If coins can be acquired through חליפין, then even with no coins in hand the owner could transfer his coins at home with a סודר. Then the friend could redeem.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a coin can be acquired through exchange, then let him transfer the coins to the other person using a cloth, and let that person redeem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רב פפא's view. If coins could be acquired through חליפין, the ברייתא would not need its trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not having coins in hand would no longer matter. With חליפין, coins can be transferred wherever they are, just by handing over a cloth. So the better method from step 2 would always be available. The fact that the ברייתא does not suggest it implies that חליפין does not work for coins.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin
Symbolic exchange. A transfer done by handing over an object.
A cloth or kerchief used to carry out חליפין
By means of, along with

phrases.english: And if you say
a coin is acquired through exchange:
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא's earlier opinion, which the גמרא is now challenging.

phrases.english: let him transfer coins to that other person
by means of a cloth, and let him redeem!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 2 to attack רב פפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's view that a coin is acquired through חליפין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חליפין worked on coins, the better method of having the friend redeem would always be possible, so the ברייתא's trick would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Answer: he has no cloth
steps.stepSummary: The defense: the ברייתא is talking about someone who has no סודר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he has no cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to defend רב פפא. It says the case is one where the man simply has no cloth to do חליפין with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer keeps רב פפא's rule in place by narrowing the ברייתא's case. The method would work in principle, but the tool for it is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not have

phrases.english: Where he has no cloth.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא should have suggested transferring the coins with a cloth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man in the ברייתא had no cloth, so he could not do that.

steps.title: Challenge: why not transfer the coins along with land?
steps.stepSummary: Even without a cloth, he could transfer the coins together with land through קנין אגב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him transfer the coins to the other person along with land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. Even without a cloth, there is another way to give the coins to the friend: along with a piece of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable things, including coins, can be acquired 'along with' land. When the land is acquired, the movables go with it. So the better method should still be available.

keyTerms.meaning: Land
Acquiring movables together with land

phrases.english: And let him transfer them to him along with land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4 by offering another method.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he has no cloth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without a cloth, קנין אגב קרקע could transfer the coins, so the better method is still possible.

steps.title: Answer: he has no land
steps.stepSummary: The defense: he owns no land either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he has no land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again narrows the case. This man owns no land at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense now describes the man as having no cloth and no land. The case is getting stranger and less realistic, and that will matter soon.

phrases.english: Where he has no land.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could have transferred the coins along with land.

steps.title: Challenge: but he is standing at a threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says he is standing at the threshing floor, which suggests he owns land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says he is standing at the threshing floor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'no land' answer using the ברייתא's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A threshing floor is land. If he is standing at his threshing floor, he does own land and could use קנין אגב. So the answer from step 6 seems to clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor
It teaches. Quoting the wording of a source.

phrases.english: But it teaches that he is standing at the threshing floor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he has no land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא places him at a threshing floor, which is land he could use.

steps.title: Answer: the threshing floor is not his
steps.stepSummary: The defense: he is standing on a threshing floor that belongs to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a threshing floor that is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends one more time. The threshing floor belongs to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the ברייתא's wording while keeping the 'no land' answer. But now the man has no money in hand, no cloth, and no land, and even the field he stands on is not his.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not his

phrases.english: On a threshing floor that is not his.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The threshing floor is his land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The threshing floor belongs to someone else.

steps.title: Would a תנא bother teaching about a man with nothing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this whole line of defense. A תנא would not go to the trouble of teaching a case about a person who owns absolutely nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would the תנא really go to such trouble just to teach us about a 'naked man' who has nothing at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and says the answers have become unbelievable. No ברייתא would be built around such a rare, empty-handed person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer on its own was possible, but together they paint a person with no coins, no cloth, and no land. A ברייתא teaches for normal situations, so this explanation is too forced. That knocks out the whole defense of רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Went to the trouble
A teacher of the משנה or ברייתא era
A 'naked man'. Someone who owns nothing.

phrases.english: And did the תנא go to all that trouble to teach us
about a naked man,
phrases.notes: Not literally naked. It just means a person with no possessions at all.

phrases.english: who has nothing at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the combined answers of steps 4, 6 and 8 as unrealistic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole chain of answers narrowing the ברייתא's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא would not be written about such a rare, possession-less person.

steps.title: Conclusion: coins are not acquired through חליפין
steps.stepSummary: Since the defense fails, the גמרא concludes that coins cannot be acquired through חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that a coin is not acquired through exchange? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes against רב פפא's earlier view. Coins cannot be transferred through חליפין, and that is why the ברייתא needed its trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reason the ברייתא did not suggest using a cloth is that a cloth does not work for coins. The question form 'אלא לאו' is followed by 'שמע מינה,' confirming the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that
Learn from it. Confirms the conclusion.

steps.whatToRemember: A coin is NOT acquired through חליפין. The proof is that the ברייתא about מעשר שני would otherwise have offered a simpler method using a סודר.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it:
a coin is not acquired through exchange.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion after the defense collapses in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אין מטבע נקנה בחליפין: coins cannot be acquired through symbolic exchange.

steps.title: רב פפא also took back his view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב פפא himself changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that רב פפא, whose view was just refuted, also changed his mind. This sets up the story that comes next as the evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the debate completely. Not only is רב פפא's earlier view rejected, but he himself came to agree with the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted, changed his mind

phrases.english: And even רב פפא retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that the person who held the refuted view agreed with the conclusion of step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא himself agreed that coins are not acquired through חליפין.

steps.title: The story: רב פפא transfers money along with his threshold
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא had 12,000 דינרים owed to him in בי חוזאי. He transferred them to רב שמואל בר אחא along with the threshold of his house, not through a cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in the case where רב פפא had twelve thousand dinars in בי חוזאי. He transferred them to רב שמואל בר אחא along with the threshold of his house. When רב שמואל בר אחא came back, רב פפא went out to greet him as far as תווך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to prove that רב פפא changed his mind. When he needed to transfer money, he used land (his threshold) instead of a cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב פפא still held that coins can be acquired through חליפין, a simple cloth would have been enough. Choosing קנין אגב קרקע shows he agreed that חליפין does not work for coins. The ending shows how pleased he was when the money was successfully brought back.

keyTerms.meaning: Dinars, coins
He transferred ownership of them
Threshold, doorstep
He went out to greet him

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that רב פפא changed not only what he said but how he acted in practice. The rule that coins are not acquired through חליפין is the accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: As in this case of רב פפא,
he had twelve thousand dinars
in בי חוזאי,
he transferred them to רב שמואל בר אחא
along with the threshold of his house.
phrases.notes: Land, not a cloth. That is the proof that רב פפא no longer used חליפין for coins.

phrases.english: When he came back,
he went out to greet him as far as תווך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence for the claim in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That רב פפא retracted his view that coins are acquired through חליפין
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב פפא's own practice of transferring money along with his threshold instead of with a cloth

steps.title: Three more authorities agree: a coin cannot be used for exchange
steps.stepSummary: עולא, רב אסי, and רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן all rule that a coin cannot serve as the item in a חליפין transaction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise עולא said: a coin cannot be used for exchange. And likewise רב אסי said the same. And likewise רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a coin cannot be used for exchange.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its conclusion by listing three more אמוראים who hold the very same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each statement repeats the same exact words, אין מטבע נעשה חליפין. Listing several big names shows this is a widely held view, not just one opinion. It also sets up the next step, where עולא's view is challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin, minted money
Exchange: a way of acquiring something by handing over an item in return
And likewise said: introduces someone who holds the same view

phrases.english: And likewise, Ulla said:
A coin cannot serve as the item for an exchange.
phrases.notes: He means a coin can't be the thing that is acquired by handing over something else in exchange.

phrases.english: And likewise, Rav Asi said:
A coin cannot serve as the item for an exchange.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: And likewise, Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A coin cannot serve as the item for an exchange.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds supporting authorities to the conclusion of steps 10 to 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coin cannot serve as the item acquired through חליפין.

steps.title: Challenge from the money changer case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges עולא from a ברייתא. Borrowing coins and repaying a little extra is allowed if the borrower has money at home, which seems to assume that coins can be acquired through חליפין. עולא is silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא challenged עולא: A man's donkey drivers and workers were demanding their pay from him in the market. He told the money changer, 'Give me a dinar's worth of coins so I can pay them, and I'll give you back a dinar and a טריסית worth from money I have at home.' If he has money at home, it is permitted. If not, it is forbidden. Now, if a coin cannot be used for exchange, it should count as a loan and be forbidden! עולא was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא brings a ברייתא that seems to show coins can be acquired through חליפין, which goes against עולא's rule. עולא has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repaying extra on a loan is ריבית. The ברייתא allows it when the man has money at home, so the money changer must be acquiring those home coins right now, through exchange, making it a deal and not a loan. If coins cannot be acquired through חליפין, nothing is acquired now, it stays a loan, and the extra should be forbidden even when he has money at home.

keyTerms.meaning: A money changer
A small coin worth less than a dinar
A loan, where extra repayment would be ריבית
He was silent, meaning he had no answer

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the coins he takes from the money changer. It is about the coins sitting at home: does the money changer acquire them right now through exchange?

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba raised an objection to Ulla:
One whose donkey drivers and workers
were demanding their pay from him in the market,
and he said to the money changer:
Give me coins worth a dinar
and I will pay them,
and I will give you back
the worth of a dinar and a tereisit
phrases.notes: The טריסית is the little extra he adds, which is why ריבית comes up.

phrases.english: from coins that I have in my house.
If he has coins at home, it is permitted,
and if not, it is forbidden.
And if you think
that a coin cannot serve as the item for an exchange,
then it is a loan, and it should be forbidden!
He was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just stated in the name of עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a coin cannot serve as חליפין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits the extra payment only when he has money at home. That only makes sense if the home coins are acquired now through exchange, which goes against עולא.

steps.title: Maybe the coins are unstamped and count as goods
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא suggests the ברייתא is talking about פרוטטות, unstamped coins. These count as a commodity, so they can be acquired through חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps both sets of coins in the ברייתא are פרוטטות, which have no stamp on them. Both sets count as goods, and that is why they can be acquired through exchange.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא offers עולא a way out. The ברייתא may be talking about unstamped coins, which are treated like goods and not like real money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's rule only covers real, minted coins. Unstamped פרוטטות are treated like goods, and goods can be acquired through חליפין. So the ברייתא fits without going against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Small coins that have not been stamped
A stamp or minting mark on a coin
Literally 'fruit': goods or a commodity, as opposed to money
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps
phrases.notes: It's רבי אבא suggesting the answer to עולא.

phrases.english: both these and those were taught about perotetot,
phrases.notes: Both means the coins at home and the coins taken from the money changer.

phrases.english: which have no stamp on them.
and both these and those count as goods,
and that is why they are acquired through exchange.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בִּפְרוּטָטוֹת שָׁנוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא is about unstamped coins.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about real minted coins, so it contradicts עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about פרוטטות, which count as goods, so חליפין works and עולא's rule stands.

steps.title: The wording of the ברייתא supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: עולא agrees and points out that the ברייתא says 'the worth of a dinar' and not 'a good dinar.' This shows it is not talking about an actual dinar coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, and the wording is precise too. It says 'the worth of a dinar and a טריסית,' and it does not say 'a good dinar and a טריסית.' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא accepts the answer and brings proof for it from the exact words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The worth of a dinar' means smaller coins that add up to a dinar's value, not a real minted dinar. That fits the idea that the coins at home are unstamped פרוטטות. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise, meaning the exact words support this
The worth of a dinar
Learn from it: the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: By the first answer, the ברייתא is about unstamped פרוטטות, which are treated as goods, so עולא's rule that real coins cannot be used for חליפין still stands.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
phrases.notes: Now it's עולא answering רבי אבא and agreeing.

phrases.english: the wording is also precise,
since it teaches: 'the worth of a dinar and a tereisit,'
and it does not teach: 'a good dinar and a tereisit.'
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 15 from the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ברייתא is talking about פרוטטות and not real coins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's wording 'יפה דינר' (the worth of a dinar) instead of 'דינר יפה' (a good dinar).

steps.title: רב אשי: it is not an exchange at all, but like 'lend me until I find the key'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the ברייתא another way. It is a deal done with money, using פרוטטות, and there is no ריבית problem because a person who has money at home is like someone asking for a short loan until his son comes or he finds his key.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, it is done with money, and about פרוטטות. Since he has money at home, it is as if he said, 'Lend me until my son comes, or until I find the key.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to רבי אבא's challenge. In his view, the ברייתא has nothing to do with חליפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer said the home coins are acquired now through exchange. רב אשי says no exchange is happening. Since the man already has the money at home, it counts like 'lend me until my son comes or I find the key,' which is not treated as a real loan, so the ריבית rules do not apply. Either way, the ברייתא does not go against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: introduces a fresh explanation
Money, a payment
Lend me
A key

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the ברייתא can be explained without any חליפין at all, so it is no proof against the rule that a coin cannot serve as חליפין.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Actually,
it is done with money, and about perotetot,
since he has money at home,
it is as if he says: Lend me
until my son comes
or until I find the key.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בְּדָמִים וּבִפְרוּטָטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the קשיא of step 14, instead of the פרוטטות-as-goods answer of steps 15 and 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the case: it is not a חליפין case but a short-term 'lend me until' situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Permission depends on the home coins being acquired now through חליפין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Having money at home makes it like 'lend me until my son comes,' which is not a real loan, so there is no ריבית and no need for חליפין.

steps.title: A משנה seems to say a coin can be used for חליפין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: anything used as payment for another item works in an exchange. The גמרא reads 'payment' as a coin and concludes a coin can be חליפין, against the ruling of עולא, רב אסי and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Anything that is used as payment for another item, once one side takes possession, the other side becomes responsible for what was given in exchange. What is 'anything used as payment for another item'? A coin. So we learn that a coin can be used for חליפין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to challenge the rule from step 13 that a coin cannot be used in a חליפין deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when something 'used as payment' is exchanged for another item, the deal closes as soon as one side takes his item. The גמרא assumes 'used as payment' means a coin. If so, coins can make a חליפין deal happen, which is exactly what עולא, רב אסי and רבי יוחנן said cannot happen.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'used as payment' must mean a coin. That is only how the challenger reads it right now, and the answer will read it differently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about loans has been answered, the גמרא brings a new challenge from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of עולא, רב אסי and רבי יוחנן that a coin cannot be used for חליפין (step 13).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה talks about something 'used as payment' working in an exchange. Read as a coin, it means coins can create חליפין.

steps.title: רב יהודה begins to reread the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה announces that he will explain what the משנה really means. The actual explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what it is saying:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the answer. רב יהודה is about to explain the משנה in a way that does not involve coins being used for חליפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'this is what it is saying' tell us the משנה will not be read the way the challenger read it. רב יהודה will offer a different reading, so the rule from step 13 can stay in place. The details come in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: a new way to read a source
